title: CHAPTER 9: IMPORTANT LABOUR LAWS IN DETAIL

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Labour Codes were framed in 2019 and 2020 to consolidate existing legislation.
The Factories Act was instituted in 1948 to safeguard industrial workers.
The Payment of Gratuity Act was introduced in 1972.
The Maternity Benefit Act of 1961 was updated with key amendments in 2017.
The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act was enacted in 2013.

blocks.content: The Government of India consolidated 44 central labour laws into 4 Labour Codes to simplify, rationalise, and modernise India's labour laws. The four codes were passed in Parliament but implementation (rules notification) is pending in many states.

cells: Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act, Payment of Bonus Act, Equal Remuneration Act
Universal minimum wage for all workers; floor wage; gender pay parity; no arbitrary deductions; monthly wage payment
Industrial Disputes Act, Trade Unions Act, Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act
Threshold for lay-off/retrenchment/closure without permission raised to 300 (from 100); recognition of single negotiating union; fixed-term employment; online return filing
EPF Act, ESI Act, Gratuity Act, Maternity Benefit Act, CMPF Act, and others (9 laws)
Gig and platform workers covered for social security; universal account number; extended social security to agricultural and informal workers
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
Factories Act, Mines Act, Plantation Labour Act, and 10 others
Working hours: 8/day, 48/week; overtime double; safety standards extended to non-factory establishments; common definitions

blocks.content: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH Act), 2013

cells: Factory = premises using power with 10+ workers; without power with 20+ workers; manufacturing process
Max 9 hours/day; 48 hours/week; no spread over more than 10.5 hours; minimum 30-minute rest after 5 hours work
Double wages for overtime work exceeding 9 hours/day or 48 hours/week; limit 50 hours/quarter
First day of week is a holiday; can be substituted but not more than 3 days consecutive work without rest day
1 day per 20 days worked for adults; 1 day per 15 days for child workers; carry forward limit
Cleanliness, disposal of waste, ventilation, temperature, lighting, drinking water, latrines, spittoons
Fencing of machinery, employment of young persons near machinery, lifting machines, pressure plant, floors and stairs
Canteen (250+ workers), creche (30+ women workers), rest rooms, first aid, safety officers (1000+ workers), welfare officer (500+ workers)
Cannot work between 7 PM and 6 AM (unless state allows with safeguards); not in dangerous operations
State Government appoints; power to enter, inspect, examine; can prohibit use of machinery
Factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port, railway company, shop, establishment with 10+ employees; once 10 employees, always applicable
On superannuation, resignation, retirement, death, or disablement; minimum 5 years continuous service (except death/disablement)
15 days salary per completed year; Last drawn salary × 15/26 × years of service (26 = working days in a month)
Rs.20 lakh (enhanced from Rs.10 lakh by 2018 amendment); may be higher under service agreement
12 months includes periods of lay-off, strike (not illegal), absence with medical certificate; seasonal workers :75 days = 1 year
Pay gratuity within 30 days of becoming payable; delayed payment attracts simple interest at prescribed rate
Gratuity can be forfeited wholly or partly for misconduct causing financial loss or wilful omission; termination for riotous/disorderly conduct
State Government appointed; receive applications; settle disputes
Gratuity up to Rs.20 lakh is tax-exempt for government employees; for others, least of: 15/26 × salary × years, Rs.20 lakh, or amount received

items: Frequently asked chronological timelines include Factories Act (1948), Payment of Gratuity Act (1972), and POSH Act (2013).
Note the primary amendment year for the Maternity Benefit Act (1961), which occurred in 2017.
Questions often cover the recent consolidation under the Labour Codes of 2019 and 2020.

cells: All establishments with 10+ employees; mines, factories, plantations, and all establishments except those covered by ESI Act
26 weeks paid leave for first 2 children (12 weeks pre-delivery + remaining post); 12 weeks for 3rd and subsequent child; 12 weeks for adoption (child below 3 months)
Must have worked at least 80 days in 12 months preceding expected delivery
Rs.3,500 if employer does not provide free medical care during pre and post-natal period
Two additional nursing breaks per day (in addition to normal rest interval) until child is 15 months old
Mandatory for establishments with 50+ employees; employer must inform women employees of crèche; 4 visits per day by mother
Employer may allow WFH after 26 weeks of maternity leave for nature of work permitting; mutually agreed terms
Punishable; void if employer dismisses woman during maternity absence; she retains all benefits
Internal Complaints Committee also covers maternity-related complaints; connect with POSH compliance

blocks.content: 9.5 Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH Act), 2013

cells: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, and Redressal) Act, 2013
Every workplace (government, private, organised, unorganised, domestic worker); all women (employees, interns, contractual, clients, customers on premises)
Unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, verbal/non-verbal/physical conduct of sexual nature, quid pro quo harassment, hostile work environment
Mandatory for establishments with 10+ employees; Presiding Officer must be senior woman employee; at least 2 employee members; 1 external member from NGO/legal background
For unorganised sector; establishment with < 10 employees; at District Collector level
Within 3 months of incident; ICC may extend by 3 months for reasonable cause
ICC must complete inquiry within 60 days; principles of natural justice; interim relief available (transfer, leave); conciliation allowed but no monetary settlement
ICC submits report to employer within 10 days of completing inquiry; employer acts within 60 days
Rs.50,000 fine for first offence; Rs.1 lakh + licence/registration cancellation for repeated offences
ICC must submit annual report to employer and District Officer; employer to include in Annual Report if company
